text: After Ehud died, the Israelites again did what was evil in the LORD's sight.
So the LORD sold them into the hand of Jabin, a Canaanite king who reigned in Hazor; his army commander was Sisera, who lived in Harosheth-hagoyim.
The Israelites cried out to the LORD, because Sisera had nine hundred iron chariots and had oppressed them cruelly for twenty years.
Deborah, a prophetess, the wife of Lappidoth, was judging Israel at that time.
She used to sit under the palm tree of Deborah, between Ramah and Bethel in the hill country of Ephraim, and the Israelites came up to her for judgment.

She sent word to Barak son of Abinoam, from Kedesh in Naphtali, and said to him, Has not the LORD, the God of Israel, commanded: Go, march to Mount Tabor, taking ten thousand men from Naphtali and Zebulun.
I will draw out Sisera, the commander of Jabin's army, along with his chariots and troops, to the river Kishon, and I will give him into your hand.
Barak answered her, If you will go with me, I will go; but if you will not go with me, I will not go.

She said, Very well, I will go with you. But know that the honor will not be yours on the road you are taking, for the LORD will sell Sisera into the hand of a woman. So Deborah got up and went with Barak to Kedesh.
Barak called Zebulun and Naphtali together at Kedesh; ten thousand men followed him, and Deborah went up with him.
Now Heber the Kenite had separated from the other Kenites, descendants of Hobab, Moses' father-in-law, and had pitched his tent as far away as the oak near Kedesh, by Zaanannim.
When Sisera was told that Barak son of Abinoam had gone up to Mount Tabor,
he called out all his nine hundred iron chariots and all the troops with him, from Harosheth-hagoyim to the river Kishon.

Then Deborah said to Barak, Get up! This is the day the LORD has given Sisera into your hand. Has not the LORD gone out ahead of you? So Barak went down from Mount Tabor, with ten thousand men following him.
At Barak's advance, the LORD threw Sisera and all his chariots and army into a panic; Sisera got down from his chariot and fled on foot.
Barak chased the chariots and the army all the way to Harosheth-hagoyim, and Sisera's whole army fell by the sword; not a single man was left.
Meanwhile Sisera fled on foot to the tent of Jael, the wife of Heber the Kenite, because there was peace between Jabin king of Hazor and the family of Heber the Kenite.
Jael came out to meet Sisera and said to him, Come in, my lord, come in here; don't be afraid. So he went into her tent, and she covered him with a rug.
He said to her, Please give me a little water to drink, for I am thirsty. She opened a skin of milk, gave him a drink, and covered him again.
He said to her, Stand at the entrance of the tent, and if anyone comes and asks you whether a man is here, say No.
But Jael, Heber's wife, took a tent peg and a hammer, went quietly to him while he was fast asleep from exhaustion, and drove the peg through his temple into the ground, and he died.

Just then Barak came by, pursuing Sisera, and Jael went out to meet him and said, Come, I will show you the man you are looking for. So he went in with her, and there lay Sisera dead, with the tent peg through his temple.
That day God subdued Jabin, the Canaanite king, before the Israelites.
And the hand of the Israelites bore down harder and harder on Jabin, the Canaanite king, until they had destroyed him.
